name: InterDigital, Inc.
description: InterDigital develops and licenses wireless, video and related technologies used in cellular (3G/4G/5G), Wi-Fi and video-compression standards. The company does not manufacture or sell any physical product; revenue comes from patent license agreements with smartphone makers, chipset/infrastructure vendors, and, increasingly, consumer-electronics and video-streaming/services companies. Licensing programs are organized as Smartphone (the largest, covering phones, tablets, base stations and other wireless devices), CE/IoT (consumer electronics and IoT/automotive products such as TVs, laptops, gaming consoles, set-top boxes and connected cars), and Video Services (an emerging program targeting SVOD/AVOD, pay-TV, video conferencing and cloud-gaming services for video-codec licensing). License agreements are typically multi-year fixed-fee or per-unit-royalty arrangements; when a new agreement is signed after a prior one has expired, InterDigital often recognizes a one-time 'catch-up' payment covering the gap period, which makes reported total revenue lumpy from quarter to quarter even though the underlying recurring royalty base is comparatively stable.

gics.industry: Communications Equipment (most common placement) or Wireless Telecommunication Services
gics.note: Conventional GICS-style box only, and it is a poor fit; see mowgliClassification. Different data providers place IDCC differently, which is itself evidence the standard boxes don't have a real home for this business model.

businessLines.name: Smartphone licensing
businessLines.description: Licensing of cellular standards-essential patents (3G/4G/5G) to smartphone, tablet, infrastructure-equipment and other wireless-device makers; InterDigital's largest program by far.
businessLines.source: web search of InterDigital FY2025 earnings coverage, 2026-09-28

businessLines.name: CE, IoT/Auto licensing
businessLines.description: Licensing of wireless and video-codec patents to consumer-electronics and IoT/automotive device makers (TVs, laptops, gaming consoles, set-top boxes, streaming devices, connected vehicles).
businessLines.revenueNote: Not independently confirmed as a standalone dollar figure in sources reviewed; annualized recurring revenue (ARR) for this program grew from ~$40 million to ~$90 million year-over-year
businessLines.source: web search of InterDigital FY2025 earnings coverage, 2026-09-28

businessLines.name: Catch-up / past-sales revenue
businessLines.description: One-time revenue recognized when a new license agreement or arbitration award retroactively covers royalties owed for a prior gap period; not a recurring revenue category but a recognition-timing feature of how licensing deals settle.
businessLines.source: web search of InterDigital FY2025 earnings coverage, 2026-09-28
